# Research questions

1. **Q1 – 1.5°C pathway**  
   How far is Costa Rica’s 2023 CO₂ per capita from a simple 2010→2050 net-zero linear path?

2. **Q2 – Peer decoupling**  
   Among countries with similar 2010 GDP per capita, does Costa Rica achieve stronger GDP growth with flat or falling CO₂ per capita?

3. **Q3 – Transport bottleneck**  
   With electricity already largely low-carbon, do transport emissions now dominate remaining CO₂ and constrain further progress?

# Data & methodology

.pull-left[

**Data sources**  
- Our World in Data CO₂ and energy datasets (1990–Latest)  
- OWID “CO₂ emissions from transport” series  
- Figures per capita unless labelled as totals  

**Analytical approach**  
- **Q1:** Compare observed CO₂ per capita to a stylised 2010–2050 linear net-zero path.  
- **Q2:** Select peers by 2010 GDP per capita; compare GDP and CO₂ per-capita changes since 2010.  
- **Q3:** Split fossil CO₂ into **transport vs all other sectors** and track their shares and per-capita trends.

]

.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:center;">
  <img src="work-flow.png" width="250" style="margin-bottom:150px;">
</div>
]


```{r include=FALSE}
# ---- Load OWID energy & CO₂ data ----

energy <- read_csv(
  "data/data_raw/owid_energy.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE)

co2 <- read_csv(
  "data/data_raw/owid_co2.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE)

# ---- Select variables used in this coursework ----
energy_sel <- energy |>
  select(
    country, iso_code, year,
    renewables_share_elec,
    low_carbon_share_elec,
    fossil_share_elec,
    renewables_electricity,
    fossil_electricity
  )

co2_sel <- co2 |>
  select(
    country, iso_code, year,
    co2,
    co2_per_capita,
    consumption_co2_per_capita,
    gdp,
    population
  )
```

### Global CO₂ Emissions per Capita (1991–2024)
Costa Rica’s per-capita emissions sit in the lower-middle of the global pack – small in totals, but not negligible compared with much larger economies((hover for country values).


```{r world-map-data, include=FALSE}
# ---- Prepare world CO₂-per-capita data for choropleth ----

co2_world <- co2_sel |>
  filter(
    year >= 1991,
    !is.na(iso_code),
    !is.na(co2),
    !is.na(co2_per_capita),
    population >= 1e6,      # drop very small states / territories
    co2_per_capita <= 50    # drop extreme outliers
  ) |>
  mutate(
    co2_pc = co2_per_capita,
    hover = if_else(
      country == "Costa Rica",
      paste0(
        "🌟 COSTA RICA 🌟<br>",
        "Year: ", year, "<br>",
        "Total CO₂: ", round(co2, 1), " Mt<br>",
        "CO₂ per capita: ", round(co2_pc, 2), " t/person"
      ),
      paste0(
        country, "<br>",
        "Year: ", year, "<br>",
        "Total CO₂: ", round(co2, 1), " Mt<br>",
        "CO₂ per capita: ", round(co2_pc, 2), " t/person"
      )
    )
  )
```


```{r world-map-plot, echo=FALSE}
# ---- Global CO₂-per-capita choropleth (animated by year) ----

fig_world_pc <- co2_world |>
  plot_ly(
    type         = "choropleth",
    locations    = ~iso_code,
    locationmode = "ISO-3",
    z            = ~co2_pc,
    zmin         = 0,
    zmax         = 25,
    frame        = ~year,
    colorscale   = "Coolwarm",
    colorbar     = list(title = "CO₂ per capita (t/person)"),
    text         = ~hover,
    hoverinfo    = "text"
  ) |>
  layout(
    geo = list(
      scope          = "world",
      projection     = list(type = "flat"),
      showframe      = FALSE,
      showcoastlines = TRUE
    )
  )

```

```{r q1_params, include=FALSE}
# ---- Q1: parameters ----
country_focus <- "Costa Rica"
pathway_start <- 2010    # baseline year for 1.5°C pathway
net_zero_year <- 2050    # year by which CO₂ per capita reaches ~0
viz_start      <- 2000   # plotting window start
year_min       <- 1990
year_max       <- 2023
```

```{r q1_series, include=FALSE}
# ---- Q1: Costa Rica CO₂ time series ----
cr_energy_co2 <- energy_sel |>
  left_join(
    co2_sel,
    by = c("country", "iso_code", "year")
  ) |>
  filter(
    country == country_focus,
    between(year, year_min, year_max)
  )
```

```{r q1_pathway, include=FALSE}
# ---- Q1: baseline and 1.5°C-compatible pathway ----
cr_base <- cr_energy_co2 |>
  filter(year == pathway_start) |>
  pull(co2_per_capita) |>
  first()

cr_pathway <- cr_energy_co2 |>
  mutate(
    co2pc_target_15c = case_when(
      year < pathway_start ~ NA_real_,
      year <= net_zero_year ~
        cr_base * pmax(
          0,
          1 - (year - pathway_start) / (net_zero_year - pathway_start)
        ),
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  )

cr_trim <- cr_pathway |>
  filter(year >= viz_start)
```

```{r q1_gap, include=FALSE}

# ---- Q1: compute gap to pathway in latest year ----
max_y       <- max(cr_trim$co2_per_capita, na.rm = TRUE)
latest_year <- max(cr_trim$year, na.rm = TRUE)

latest_values <- cr_trim |>
  filter(year == latest_year) |>
  summarise(
    gap = co2_per_capita - co2pc_target_15c,
    pct = gap / co2pc_target_15c
  )

gap_value <- latest_values$gap[1]
pct_value <- latest_values$pct[1]

pct_label <- if (is.finite(pct_value)) {
  percent(pct_value, accuracy = 1)
} else {
  "n/a"
}

gap_label <- sprintf(
  "%d gap: %+0.2f t/person\n(%s above pathway)",
  latest_year,
  gap_value,
  pct_label
)
```

```{r q1_plot_object, include=FALSE}

# ---- Q1: plot object ----
p1 <- ggplot(cr_trim, aes(x = year)) +
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = pathway_start, xmax = latest_year,
    ymin = -Inf,          ymax = Inf,
    fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = co2pc_target_15c),
    colour    = "#D55E00",
    linewidth = 1.1,
    linetype  = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = co2_per_capita),
    colour    = "#1A1A1A",
    linewidth = 1.4
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x     = pathway_start + 10,
    y     = max_y * 0.45,
    label = gap_label,
    hjust = 0,
    size  = 4,
    colour = "red"
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype   = "dotted",
    colour     = "grey60"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = pathway_start,
    linetype   = "dashed",
    colour     = "grey50"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x     = pathway_start,
    y     = 0.15,
    label = "2010 baseline",
    angle = 90,
    vjust = -0.3,
    hjust = 0,
    size  = 3,
    colour = "grey40"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Costa Rica's CO₂ per capita vs a 1.5°C-compatible pathway",
    subtitle = "Stylised linear net-zero path (2010–2050) compared with observed emissions",
    x        = "Year",
    y        = "CO₂ emissions per capita (tonnes/person)",
    caption  = "Source: Our World in Data – CO₂ and Energy datasets."
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, max_y * 1.05)) +
  theme_clean(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position   = "none",
    panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major  = element_line(colour = "grey90"),
    plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle     = element_text(size = 11, colour = "#555555")
  )
```

# Q1 – Is Costa Rica on a 1.5°C path?
Costa Rica’s 2023 CO₂ per capita is ~50% above the stylised 1.5°C-compatible pathway, implying deeper cuts are now required.

```{r q1_plot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=6, fig.width=14}
ggplotly(p1)
```


```{r q2_peers, include=FALSE}
# ---- Q2: peer selection based on 2010 GDP per capita ----

peer_band <- 0.30   # ±30% GDP band for scatter peers

# 2010 GDP per capita for Costa Rica
cr_2010 <- co2_sel |>
  filter(country == country_focus, year == 2010) |>
  filter(!is.na(gdp), !is.na(population)) |>
  mutate(gdp_pc_2010 = gdp / population) |>
  slice(1)

cr_gdp_pc_2010 <- cr_2010$gdp_pc_2010[1]

# Candidate pool with GDP differences
peer_candidates <- co2_sel |>
  filter(year == 2010, !is.na(gdp), !is.na(population)) |>
  mutate(
    gdp_pc_2010 = gdp / population,
    diff        = abs(gdp_pc_2010 - cr_gdp_pc_2010)
  )

# Scatter peers: all countries within ±30% band
peer_band_countries <- peer_candidates |>
  filter(
    country != country_focus,
    between(
      gdp_pc_2010,
      cr_gdp_pc_2010 * (1 - peer_band),
      cr_gdp_pc_2010 * (1 + peer_band)
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(diff) |>
  pull(country)

q2_countries_scatter <- unique(c(country_focus, peer_band_countries))
```

```{r q2_decouple_summary, include=FALSE}
# ---- Q2: summary of GDP and CO₂ changes since 2010 (for scatter) ----

decouple_df <- co2_sel |>
  filter(
    country %in% q2_countries_scatter,
    year >= 2010,
    !is.na(gdp), !is.na(population),
    !is.na(co2_per_capita)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    gdp_per_capita = gdp / population
  )

summary_decouple <- decouple_df |>
  group_by(country) |>
  arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    gdp_pc_change = 100 * (last(gdp_per_capita) / first(gdp_per_capita) - 1),
    co2_pc_change = 100 * (last(co2_per_capita)   / first(co2_per_capita) - 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(gdp_pc_change))
```

```{r q2_scatter_data, include=FALSE}

q2_scatter <- summary_decouple |>
  mutate(
    highlight  = country == country_focus,
    hover_text = sprintf(
      "Country: %s<br>GDP change: %+.1f%%<br>CO\u2082 change: %+.1f%%",
      country,
      gdp_pc_change,
      co2_pc_change
    )
  )
```


```{r q2_scatter_object, include=FALSE}
# ---- Q2: scatter plot Object ----

q2_scatter_gg <- 
  ggplot(q2_scatter, aes(x = gdp_pc_change, y = co2_pc_change)) +
  
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey75") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey75") +
  
  geom_point(
    data  = filter(q2_scatter, !highlight),
    aes(text = hover_text),
    colour = "#AEB6C4",
    size   = 2.8,
    alpha  = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data  = filter(q2_scatter, highlight),
    aes(text = hover_text),
    colour = "#D55E00",
    size   = 4
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data  = filter(q2_scatter, highlight),
    aes(label = country),
    colour  = "#D55E00",
    size    = 4,
    seed    = 123,
    box.padding = 0.4
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "GDP vs CO₂ per capita change since 2010",
    x     = "GDP per capita change (%)",
    y     = "CO₂ per capita change (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) 
  
```

# Q2 – GDP vs CO₂ change since 2010
Costa Rica delivers ~32% GDP per capita growth while keeping CO₂ per capita just below 2010 levels—better than many similar-income peers but not unique.

```{r q2_scatter_plot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=6, fig.width=14}
ggplotly(q2_scatter_gg, tooltip = "text")
```
```{r q3_data, include=FALSE}
# ---- Q3: Transport vs other CO₂ for Costa Rica ----

transport <- read_csv(
  "https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/co2-emissions-transport.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

transport_cr <- transport |>
  rename(
    country       = 1,   # "Entity"
    iso_code      = 2,   # "Code"
    year          = 3,   # "Year"
    transport_co2 = 4    # CO₂ from transport, **tonnes**
  ) |>
  filter(country == country_focus)

cr_transport <- co2_sel |>
  filter(country == country_focus, year >= 1990) |>
  select(country, iso_code, year, co2, co2_per_capita, population) |>
  left_join(transport_cr, by = c("country", "iso_code", "year")) |>
  mutate(
    # co2 is in million tonnes; transport_co2 is in tonnes
    transport_share_total = if_else(
      !is.na(co2) & co2 > 0,
      transport_co2 / (co2 * 1e6),   # <-- CORRECT: tonnes / tonnes
      NA_real_
    ),
    transport_co2_pc     = transport_co2 / population,          # t/person
    non_transport_co2_pc = ((co2 * 1e6) - transport_co2) / population  # t/person
  )

cr_trans_share <- cr_transport |>
  filter(!is.na(transport_share_total))

cr_pc_long <- cr_transport |>
  filter(!is.na(transport_co2_pc)) |>
  select(year, transport_co2_pc, non_transport_co2_pc) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(transport_co2_pc, non_transport_co2_pc),
    names_to  = "sector",
    values_to = "co2_pc"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    sector = recode(
      sector,
      transport_co2_pc     = "Transport",
      non_transport_co2_pc = "All other sectors"
    )
  )
```


```{r q3_share_plot_obj, include=FALSE}
# ---- Q3: plot – transport share of total CO₂ ----

p3 <- ggplot(cr_trans_share, aes(x = year)) +
  
  # reference line for "half of emissions"
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 50,
    linetype   = "dashed",
    colour     = "grey70"
  ) +
  
  geom_line(
    aes(y = transport_share_total * 100),
    colour    = "#D55E00",
    linewidth = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(y = transport_share_total * 100),
    colour = "#D55E00"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Transport’s share of Costa Rica’s CO₂ emissions",
    x     = "Year",
    y     = "Transport share of total CO₂ (%)"
  ) +
  theme_clean(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r q3_decomp_plot_obj, include=FALSE}
# ---- Q3: plot – CO₂ per capita from transport vs other sectors ----

p4 <- ggplot(cr_pc_long, aes(x = year, y = co2_pc, colour = sector)) +
  
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    "Transport"         = "#D55E00",
    "All other sectors" = "#0072B2"
  )) +
  labs(
    title  = "CO₂ per capita from transport vs other sectors",
    x      = "Year",
    y      = "Tonnes CO₂ per person",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_clean(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

```

# Q3 – Has transport become the main bottleneck?
By 2020s, ~70–75% of Costa Rica’s fossil CO₂ comes from transport – almost everything left is on the road.
```{r q3_share_plot, echo=FALSE}
ggplotly(p3)
```

---
# Q3 – CO₂ per capita: transport vs other sectors

Other sectors decline or flatten; transport hardly falls, making it the main brake on further progress
```{r q3_decomp_plot, echo=FALSE}
ggplotly(p4)
```

### Discussion

.pull-left[

- **Q1 – 1.5°C pathway**  
  Costa Rica sits ~50% above a simple 1.5°C-consistent path by 2023,  
  meaning recent cuts are not steep enough.

- **Q2 – Relative decoupling**  
  ~32% GDP per-capita growth with flat or slightly falling emissions —  
  better than many peers but not exceptional.

- **Q3 – Transport bottleneck**  
  Transport now contributes ~70–75% of fossil CO₂, and other sectors  
  provide limited additional reductions.

- **Limitations**  
  Results depend on a stylised per-capita pathway, the peer group  
  definition, and production-based CO₂ metrics.
  
]

### Conclusion – Is Costa Rica’s transition fast enough for 1.5°C?

.pull-left[
- **Verdict:**  
  Costa Rica is ~50% above a simple 1.5°C pathway by 2023.  
  The transition is **not fast enough**.

- **Relative performance:**  
  Stronger than many similar-income peers,  
  but “better than peers” ≠ **1.5°C-compatible**.

- **Implication:**  
  With electricity already low-carbon,  
  **transport now determines the national trajectory**.
]
